1.title: The Troubleshooting Methodology
1.text: Welcome to Module twenty: The Troubleshooting Methodology. It covers the exam area five point zero Network Troubleshooting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. five point one Explain the troubleshooting methodology: identify the problem. Establish a theory of probable cause. Test the theory to determine the cause. Establish a plan of action and identify potential effects. Implement the solution or escalate. Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five point zero Network Troubleshooting (twenty-four percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: The seven steps
1.text: The seven steps. The figure shows this: The Comp T I A troubleshooting methodology as an ordered loop.

1.title: The seven steps, continued
1.text: The seven steps. one. Step: Identify the problem. What you do: Gather information, question users, identify symptoms, determine whether anything has changed, duplicate the problem if possible, approach multiple problems individually. two. Step: Establish a theory of probable cause. What you do: Question the obvious; consider multiple approaches: top-to-bottom or bottom-to-top O S I, divide and conquer. three. Step: Test the theory to determine the cause. What you do: If confirmed, determine next steps; if not confirmed, establish a new theory or escalate.

1.title: The seven steps, continued
1.text: The seven steps. four. Step: Establish a plan of action. What you do: Plan the fix and identify potential effects (impact, rollback). five. Step: Implement the solution or escalate. What you do: Make the change, or escalate if outside your authority or skill. six. Step: Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures. What you do: Confirm the fix and that nothing else broke; prevent a repeat. seven. Step: Document findings, actions, outcomes and lessons learned. What you do: Record everything, throughout the process. Exam tip: Memorize the order. Testing the theory comes before the plan of action; documentation is last (and continues throughout).

1.title: Approaches
1.text: Approaches. Top-to-bottom O S I. Start at the application layer and work down. Bottom-to-top O S I. Start at the physical layer (cables, link lights) and work up. Divide and conquer. Start at the layer you suspect, then go up or down. Question the obvious. Is it plugged in? Is the port enabled? Is the interface up?

1.title: Practical habits
1.text: Practical habits. Ask what changed. Most outages follow a change. Change one thing at a time. You know what fixed it. Duplicate the problem. Confirms the symptom and tests the fix. Escalate when needed. Do not guess beyond your authority. Exam tip: "Users report the issue after a weekend maintenance" equals ask what changed first. Change one variable at a time. Exam tip: Test the theory before you plan the fix; document throughout and last.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A user cannot reach a file server. The technician asks the user what error appeared and whether anything changed recently. Which step is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Identify the problem. Gathering information and asking about changes is the first step.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. After forming a theory, what should the technician do next? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Test the theory to determine the cause. The theory must be tested before acting.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. The technician's theory is not confirmed. What should be done next? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Establish a new theory or escalate. If the theory fails, form a new one or escalate.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A technician starts at the physical layer by checking cables and link lights, then moves up. Which approach is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Bottom-to-top O S I. Starting at layer one and moving up is bottom-to-top.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. After the fix, the technician confirms users can work and checks that no other service broke. Which step is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures. Verification follows implementation.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which step happens throughout the process and also at the very end? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Documenting findings, actions and outcomes. Documentation continues from start to finish.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many steps does the methodology have? Answer: Seven. Question two. What is the first step? Answer: Identify the problem. Question three. What is divide and conquer? Answer: Starting at the layer you suspect and working up or down.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What should you determine about the environment first? Answer: Whether anything has changed. Question five. What comes after testing the theory when it is confirmed? Answer: Determine the next steps and establish a plan of action. Question six. What is the last step? Answer: Document findings, actions, outcomes and lessons learned.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Step: Key action. one: identify the problem (gather, question, symptoms, changes, duplicate). two: theory of probable cause (obvious, O S I approaches, divide and conquer). three: test the theory (confirmed or new theory or escalate). four: plan of action with potential effects. five: implement or escalate. six: verify and prevent. seven: document.
